findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_earnings_call_transcript · Private data: get_company_insider_transactions · Public sink: get_share_price, get_price_history, get_holder_holdings.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_earnings_call_transcript · Private data: get_company_insider_transactions · Public sink: get_share_price, get_price_history, get_holder_holdings

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_company" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Use this when you need to identify a public company on 6ix by ticker or name before asking for its news releases or events. Returns matching companies with ticker, exchange and their 6ix page." → after: "Use this when a ticker or company name is ambiguous and you need the exact listed company first. Give it a ticker or name. Returns matching companies with ticker, exchange and their 6ix.com page; the other tools also accept a ticker or name directly."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
